**Re-post after the plan v5 §4 stub authorization. Supersedes v3 (`PASS_PARTIAL

## Read this first: the grant path is documented as UNWIRED, so this token is a judgment call

SKILL.md:4515's `PASS_PARTIAL` row offers exactly two resolutions — "resolve them in the diff, OR
re-authorize the stubs in §4 Design (**canary-like exception, not yet wired**)" — and
workflow.yaml:1624 says the same thing as "(canary-like exception, **v1.1**)". I took the second
resolution; plan v5 §4 now authorizes both stubs with per-arm compensating controls. But the
routing table has only four tokens (`PASS_UNIFIED`, `PASS_CANARY`, `PASS_PARTIAL`,
`FAIL_NO_CANARY`) and **none of them is the authorized-stub grant**. So there is no mechanical
token that expresses "stubs authorized at plan time". Whatever I post here is an orchestrator
judgment on an unimplemented path, and it should be read as such rather than as a gate that
mechanically cleared. A `kind: infra` workflow-fix task is filed for the missing grant token.

## Why `PASS_UNIFIED` and not the alternatives

- **`PASS_PARTIAL` again** would be self-defeating: the routing table maps it to REFUSE, so
  re-posting it after taking the routing table's own sanctioned resolution makes the gate
  unsatisfiable. That is not what the gate says.
- **`PASS_CANARY`** would require me to assert that the smoke and sweep **paths diverge** (the
  in-process-vs-subprocess class the token was built for, #397). Ours do not: smoke IS the
  production driver under `--smoke`, same phased CLI, same staging helpers, same upload surface.
  Claiming divergence to buy a grant would be a false statement in a durable marker.
- **`PASS_UNIFIED`** asserts two things, both true here: the architecture is unified end-to-end,
  AND every planned arm resolves REAL or N/A. The second clause is the one that changed, and only
  because §4 changed — see the next section.

## What changed about the two arms (this is the honest part)

Nothing about the CODE changed. What changed is that the plan now declares these arms
non-smoke-executable **by design, reviewed at plan time**. That is exactly the distinction the
gate exists to enforce (#397 rationale: "forces the divergence to be explicit at plan time so the
pre-dispatch moment catches it").

The contract defines FALLBACK as "a stub / bias-refit / early-return **in place of** the arm's
production computation path" — the #1689 harm class where a stub silently delivered *arms of the
wrong science*. Under plan v4 these two arms were unauthorized gaps between what the plan expected
and what smoke exercised, so FALLBACK was the correct row and `PASS_PARTIAL` the correct token.
Under v5 they are declared-and-reviewed non-executions, and nothing downstream consumes a
substitute result from either: `--skip-upload` runs no verification at all rather than a fake
passing one, and the GPU cell simply does not execute.

I want this recorded plainly because the reclassification is the load-bearing step and it would be
easy to dress up: **N/A here means "authorized, plan-reviewed non-execution", not "verified".**

## Residual untested seams — named, not waived

1. **GPU device routing in `confirm-b-gpu`** never executed anywhere (torch device placement,
   cusolver fp64 path). Bounded: it runs on a SEPARATE conditional provision (`pod-2163-b`), not
   the main ~6 h CPU workload; it shares its fit kernel with the CPU `confirm-b` arm that ran REAL
   at smoke (22 s); it self-gates on an on-device eigh(8,192) pilot before committing the full
   factorization; and plan §12 A4's census extrapolation (~38k raw distinct pre-floor, strictly
   shrunk by the ≥20-row floor, vs the >~32,768 trigger) rates it unlikely to fire at all.
2. **Real HF interaction in `upload-verify`** never executed. Bounded: the three call sites are
   autospec-pinned by unit tests in the reviewed diff; `stage_hub_prefix` /
   `verify_repo_paths_uploaded` are shared mature helpers, not new code; and the standing
   never-terminate-before-uploads-verify rule means a broken upload surfaces as a FAILED verify
   rather than as data loss.
